answer: Here is a specific defense: chain each registration to a per-identity nonce derived from the prior epoch hash so clones collide. Anomalous synchrony in submission timestamps is a hard tell. Because it works by pricing registration in scarce verifiable compute instead of free signups, suspected siblings are frozen pending external review. An identity earns only when its tide recurs, its mesa survives audit, and a orchard from an unlinked peer confirms it.
